findings.description: A partial pass that dies or cannot post now sets no failure status, because the `if (partial)` branch runs before the `failure` branch. That contradicts README L127 ("A run that dies ... fails the check"). Statuses are also per SHA, so after a push a partial pass leaves `claude-review` absent on the new head, which a required check reads as "waiting". Neither case is documented. Either set `failure` on a failed partial pass and skip only `success`, or document both.

The lock comment (and its twin in templates/github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml) calls the built-in read-only commands "a set no setting changes". The matrix row says an `ask` or `deny` rule changes it, and the lock's own managed `Bash(git *--output*)` deny already narrows the read-only git forms. Reword to "a set only a managed ask or deny rule narrows".

A relocated suggestion now goes through `inertFences`, so it is no longer posted as written. `<pre` gets an invisible U+200B, which breaks pasted JSX or HTML, and ```` ```ts title ```` becomes ```` ```text ts title ````. Yet the comment at L53-54 still says it "is posted exactly as written", and L57 still says "Same text".

The new relocated-suggestion test would pass even without its open-fence body, and it checks only for a backtick `suggestion` fence line. A tilde `~~~suggestion`, a `> ```suggestion`, or a `<pre lang="suggestion">` after an open `<textarea>` in the body would all go uncaught. Add cases for these to pin the protection down.

SKILL.md lists the built-in read-only commands as `ls, cat, head, tail, grep, find, wc, cd` and then says "nothing else", but the matrix row also lists `echo`, `pwd`, `diff`, `stat`, `du` and `which`. Make the two lists match, or mark the SKILL.md list as examples.
`commentBody` tests `relocated` twice, in two ternaries, to pair an inert fence with inert text. An `if (relocated)` / `else` that pushes each case whole would keep the pairing in one place.
The edited `@claude review` bullet's second line runs well past the ~100-column wrap of the lines around it. Rewrap so `deep` starts a new line.

The reflowed lock comment leaves one over-long line ("# off. None of the verbs writes: ... so a PR whose diff") among lines wrapped near 80 columns, in both this file and its template twin. Rewrap from `off.` onward.

process_issues.description: As in the prior round, `.claude-pr/` held only CLAUDE.md, with no AGENTS.md, .agents or templates, even though RESTORE_PATHS names them. Reviewers were told to read the PR's copies with `git show HEAD:<path>` instead.

Each area ran a single instance even though the delta touches 17 files across several top-level areas, which the file-count size gate would scale to 2. Only about 30 lines of logic changed and the rest is prose, so a second instance would have added nothing.
